page: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, alongside 1843 GB of bundled local storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-threaded and memory performance. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 50,758.8 and a PassMark memory score of 2,826.39, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 221.85 GB/sec, and database operations scored 23,567.62, highlighting robust data-processing capabilities. However, compute-heavy tasks such as large-scale LLM text generation performed poorly at 2.33 tokens/sec, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E48bds_v5 offers a dense resource profile by bundling substantial local storage with a large memory footprint, reducing the need for external premium block storage for temporary data. This makes the server highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers, data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high memory throughput and local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EBDSv5 family, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs, 384.0 GB of RAM, and 1843 GB of bundled local storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance delivers strong performance in memory-bound and database operations, as evidenced by its high PassMark memory and database benchmark scores. While it excels at multi-threaded decompression and data processing, its lack of GPU acceleration limits its efficiency for large-scale AI model inference. The combination of high memory density and local storage makes it a cost-effective solution for enterprise databases, in-memory analytics, and memory-heavy workloads.
